title: Payroll Services Cost: 2026 Prices by Team Size
summary: How much do payroll services cost? See 2026 prices for Homebase, Gusto, and QuickBooks at 5 to 30 employees, plus the hidden fees to ask about before you sign.
body_markdown:
Payroll services for small businesses cost about $110 to $200 a month for a 10-person team, depending on the provider and plan you pick. That price comes from two parts: a monthly base fee and a fee for each employee you pay. Your headcount, how often you run payroll, and add-ons like faster deposits can push the total higher.


To help you get the most features for your budget, below we compare payroll services cost for teams of 5 to 30 employees with Homebase, Gusto, and QuickBooks, what the base price should include, and the fees that tend to show up after you sign.


*Prices verified November 2026.*


## Payroll Services Cost at a Glance (November 2026)


- When budgeting for payroll services, keep in mind that most charge a monthly base fee plus a fee for each employee you pay.
- Published small business plans range from about $35 to $180 a month in base fees and $5 to $22 per employee.
- A 10-person team pays about $110 to $200 a month on entry-level and mid-tier plans.
- Homebase Payroll costs $49 a month plus $6 per employee paid, with unlimited payroll runs and tax filing included.
- Ask about fees for faster deposits, multi-state payroll, time tracking, and year-end tax forms before you sign.

## How Much Do Payroll Services Cost?


In our research, we found that payroll services usually cost a monthly base fee of about $35 to $180 plus $5 to $22 per employee paid. For 5 to 30 employees, entry-level full-service plans run about $80 to $260 a month (we updated these numbers as of November 2026). Faster deposits, multi-state payroll, and HR tools cost more.


Here are a few different fee types and pricing models to keep in mind:


### Base Fees


The base fee is a flat monthly charge for your payroll account. The base fee typically covers the app, tax filing, and support whether you pay three people or 30.


On published small business plans, base fees start around $35 with Square (point of sale app) and run up to $180 with Gusto Premium. Most entry-level full-service plans, including Homebase, Gusto Simple, and QuickBooks Workforce Payroll, sit at about $49.


### Per-Employee Fees


On top of the base fee, most providers charge for each person you pay that month, usually $5 to $22 per employee. Many count only the people who get a paycheck, not everyone on your roster. That matters if your headcount rises and falls with the seasons.


For example, paying 12 people with Homebase costs $49 plus 12 × $6, or $121 for the month.


### Pricing Models: Base Plus Per Employee, Flat Rate, and Custom Quotes


- **Base fee plus per employee.** This is the most common model. Your bill grows a little with each hire, and you can work out the price before you sign.
- **Flat rate.** One price regardless of headcount. It's less common for payroll and usually comes with a team-size cap.
- **Custom quote.** You get a price after a sales call. It's common with larger providers and makes side-by-side comparisons harder.


**One thing to watch:** per-location pricing usually describes scheduling or time tracking plans, not payroll. At Homebase, scheduling plans are priced per location, and payroll is priced per employee paid.


## What's Included in a Full-Service Payroll Plan


A full-service payroll plan should handle the work that keeps you compliant, not only the paycheck math.


Here's what to expect in the base price:


- Paycheck calculations, including overtime, deductions, and withholding.
- Direct deposit for your team.
- Federal, state, and local payroll tax filing and payments.
- W-2 and 1099 forms at the end of the year.
- New hire reporting to your state.
- Unlimited payroll runs, so a bonus or final paycheck doesn't cost extra.
- Online access for employees to view pay stubs and tax forms.


If a quote lists tax filing as an add-on, ask why. It's standard in full-service plans, and it's the part of payroll that carries the biggest penalties when it's late.

The headline price rarely covers everything. These are the fees that most often raise the cost of payroll services for small businesses:

Before you sign, ask the sales rep:


1. Is federal and state tax filing included?
2. Are payroll runs unlimited, including bonus and final paychecks?
3. What do faster deposits cost?
4. Do you charge for W-2s and 1099s?
5. What does it cost to switch providers in the middle of the year?

## Payroll Services Cost for Small Business: In-House vs. Outsourced


Running payroll in-house means paying for someone's time and carrying the risk of mistakes. A bookkeeping clerk earns a median of $24.36 an hour, and a late payroll tax deposit can cost 2% to 15% of the amount due. A full-service plan for 10 employees runs about $110 a month.


- **Time.** Even with a good spreadsheet, payroll can take hours each pay period: collecting timecards, calculating overtime, working out withholding, and making tax deposits. If you're outsourcing that time, factor in the cost. At the[Bureau of Labor Statistics median pay for bookkeeping clerks](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/office-and-administrative-support/bookkeeping-accounting-and-auditing-clerks.htm) , $24.36 an hour as of May 2025, three hours a week comes to about $315 a month in labor.
- **Risk.** The[IRS charges a failure-to-deposit penalty](https://www.irs.gov/payments/failure-to-deposit-penalty) when payroll taxes land late: 2% for deposits one to five days late, 5% for six to 15 days, 10% after 15 days, and 15% if the amount is still unpaid 10 days after an IRS notice. On a $5,000 deposit, even the lowest tier costs $100.
- **A third option.** A professional employer organization (PEO) runs payroll and also handles benefits and HR as a co-employer. It usually costs more than a payroll service, so it fits teams that want benefits administration handled too.


> "I was actually manually calculating if someone clocked in at 8:01 and worked until 3:15. You're wasting so much time on things that are so frivolous and you have to really as a small business owner dedicate that to more important tasks."
>
>
> Primo Stropoli, Owner, Tetta's Market


Today, Primo says payroll takes him about five minutes a week.


## What Payroll Costs Look Like for Hourly and Tipped Teams


Payroll for hourly teams has more moving parts than payroll for a salaried team, and each one takes time when hours are entered by hand:


- **More frequent runs.** Many hourly teams pay weekly or every two weeks, so any fee tied to each run adds up faster.
- **Overtime across wage rates.** A shift lead who also covers a cashier shift may earn two rates in one week, and overtime has to be calculated across both.
- **Tips.** Tipped employees need tips reported, pooled, and added to their paychecks.
- **Seasonal swings.** Headcount rises and falls, so pricing based on employees paid keeps your bill in line with your team.


The fix is connecting time tracking to payroll. When hours come straight from the time clock, overtime and breaks are calculated before payroll runs, and nobody retypes timecards. With Homebase, approved timesheets feed payroll directly, and[Tip Manager](https://www.joinhomebase.com/tip-manager) ($25 a month per location) pulls tips from your POS, calculates the tip pool, and adds it to timesheets.


> "I ran payroll last night for the whole company and I clicked on everyone's names because it was like crazy overtime for everybody in the last two weeks... It's just so clear-cut to see the breakdown, and if you ever have to edit it, you just unlock the time sheet."
>
>
> Cherie Chua, Co-Founder and Creative Director, Luxe Bites


## How to Lower Your Payroll Services Cost


1. **Pay only for the employees you pay.** Pick a provider that charges per employee paid each month, not per person on your roster. Seasonal teams feel the difference most.
2. **Match the plan to how you run payroll.** If your whole team works in one state and you already track time elsewhere, you may not need a higher tier. If you do need multi-state payroll or time tracking, compare the full price, not just the base plan.
3. **Connect time tracking to payroll.** Hours that flow from the time clock cut down on correction runs, late deposits, and back pay for missed overtime.
4. **Choose annual billing where it's offered.** Homebase scheduling plans cost less billed annually. Essentials is $24 a month billed annually, compared with $30 billed monthly.


## Payroll Services Cost FAQs


### How much do payroll services cost?


Most small business payroll services charge a monthly base fee of about $35 to $180 plus $5 to $22 per employee paid. For a 10-person team, published plans from Homebase, Gusto, and QuickBooks run about $110 to $200 a month as of November 2026. Faster deposits, multi-state filing, and HR tools add more.


### How much does Homebase payroll cost?


Homebase Payroll costs $49 a month plus $6 per employee paid, with unlimited payroll runs, automated tax filing, W-2s and 1099s, and direct deposit included. Next-Day Payroll costs $59 a month plus $9 per employee paid. You can add payroll to any Homebase plan, including the free Basic plan.


### How much does Gusto payroll cost?


Gusto's Simple plan costs $49 a month plus $6 per person, Plus costs $80 plus $12 per person, and Premium costs $180 plus $22 per person. Simple covers payroll in one state only, and time tracking comes with Plus, so multi-state teams and teams that want built-in time tracking usually need Plus.


### How much does QuickBooks payroll cost?


QuickBooks Workforce Payroll costs $50 a month plus $7 per employee. Workforce Premium, which adds time tracking and HR tools, costs $88 plus $13 per employee, and Workforce Elite costs $134 plus $17 per employee. Intuit often runs introductory discounts, so check the regular price before you compare.


### How much does it cost to outsource payroll?


Outsourcing to a full-service payroll provider costs about $80 to $260 a month for a team of 5 to 30 on entry-level plans from Homebase, Gusto, and QuickBooks. A professional employer organization (PEO), which also handles benefits and HR, usually costs more because you're paying for those services too.


### Are payroll services worth it?


For most small businesses, yes. A full-service plan for 10 employees costs about $110 a month, while one late payroll tax deposit can trigger an IRS penalty of 2% to 15% of the amount due. Payroll services also calculate overtime and withholding for you, which cuts the errors that lead to back pay.


### What's included in full-service payroll?


Full-service payroll usually includes paycheck calculations, direct deposit, federal and state payroll tax filing and payments, W-2 and 1099 forms, and new hire reporting. Some providers charge extra for faster deposits, multi-state filing, time tracking, or year-end forms, so confirm what's in the base price before you compare.


## Find the Payroll Service That Fits Your Budget


The right payroll service is the one whose full monthly total fits your team, not the one with the lowest base fee. Price it out at your real headcount, confirm tax filing and year-end forms are in the base price, and ask about every fee in the checklist above before you sign.
